To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a normalized Schur-Cohen test in the discrete domain is transformed into a new delta-operator-based test, that is a smooth transition between the discrete and continuous domains, and that this test is a generalization of the Pham-Le-Breton test.
we have proposed a new delta-operator-based zero location test, and that it is the limit of the discrete-time normalized Schur-Cohen test as the sampling time goes to zero.

the new test is the normalized Schur–Cohn test in the delta-operator domain, that its limit as the sampling interval tends to zero is the Pham-Le-Breton test in the continuous-time, and that the test is more accurate for small sampling intervals than the discrete-time normalized Schur– Cohn test.
